Title: Chief signs in with the permanent password and lands in the Chief Examiner workspace
Preconditions: Chief account provisioned by the Chairman; first-time password set already completed; WEB_APP_URL set
Steps: 1) Open WEB_APP_URL; 2) Enter the chief email and permanent password; 3) Click Sign in; 4) Wait for the shell to render
Expected Result: Authenticated shell renders with the Primary navigation sidebar; no first-time Set your password prompt appears again
Notes: signInRole('chief') must resolve to state shell; covered by tests/web/testcases/chief-examiner.spec.ts CHF-01

Title: Chief sidebar exposes exactly the seven documented Chief modules
Preconditions: Chief signed in with an unlocked subject scope
Steps: 1) Read the Primary navigation landmark; 2) Compare the module buttons with utils/dvsRoles.ts
Expected Result: Allocation engine, Evaluator master, Manage team, Attendance, Moderation, Moderation reports and Live monitoring are all visible
Test Data: modules from the DVS_ROLES entry with role=chief
Notes: Spec CHF-02; an extra undocumented module should be reported rather than ignored

Title: Chief sidebar hides every other role's modules
Preconditions: Chief signed in
Steps: 1) Read the Primary navigation landmark; 2) Count Exam configuration, Marking schemes, Access governance, Chief nominations, Chief master, Evaluation desk, Digitization and User management
Expected Result: Every foreign module renders zero buttons; no foreign workspace is reachable from the shell
Notes: Spec CHF-03 covers Exam configuration, Access governance and Evaluation desk; extend to the remaining role labels

Title: API reports the Chief evaluator grade
Preconditions: Chief signed in through ApiSession
Steps: 1) Sign in with ApiSession; 2) GET /api/v1/auth/me
Expected Result: evaluator_grade equals chief and the role matches the Chief Examiner workspace
Notes: Spec CHF-04

Title: Unauthenticated Chief summary read is refused
Preconditions: No session cookie or token held by the caller
Steps: 1) Create an API context with no storage state; 2) GET /api/v1/chief/summary
Expected Result: 401 (403 accepted only if the tenant answers anonymous calls that way); no summary body is returned
Notes: Spec CHF-05 asserts 401/403; a 200 with a payload is an S1 defect

Title: Chief cannot read the admin security and governance catalog
Preconditions: Chief signed in with an unlocked scope
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/security/catalog; 2) GET /api/v1/auth/security-context
Expected Result: 403 on the governance catalog; no policy, membership or centre data is disclosed
Notes: Verify the chief role is refused (403) on the security catalog and that security-context exposes no admin policy fields

Title: Chief cannot open the evaluator marking workspace
Preconditions: An assignment exists in the chief's own batch; chief signed in
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/marking/assignments/{assignmentId}/workspace; 2) POST /api/v1/marking/assignments/{assignmentId}/open
Expected Result: 403 on both calls; no workspace, marks or script pages are disclosed
Test Data: assignment id from the chief's own batch
Notes: Verify the chief role is refused on Routes.MARKING_WORKSPACE and Routes.MARKING_OPEN; moderation samples have their own viewer route

Title: Chief summary returns every documented counter
Preconditions: Chief signed in with at least one accepted subject
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/chief/summary; 2) Validate the payload against the captured schema
Expected Result: profile (name, code, email, institution, department, experience), evaluation (total, submitted, in_progress), ready, subjects, attendance, present, team_size, moderation_pending, ai_evaluation_mode, nominations and generated_at are all present
Notes: Validate with AJV against the captured schema

Title: Chief summary subject scope equals the accepted nominations exactly
Preconditions: At least one completed and one pending nomination exist
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/chairman/my-nominations; 2) GET /api/v1/chief/summary; 3) Diff the subject id sets
Expected Result: summary.subjects ids equal the ids of nominations with status completed; no extra and no missing subject
Test Data: nomination ids from the run state
Notes: Verify the set equality in both directions, including that a pending subject never appears in the scope

Title: A chief that was never nominated stays locked with an empty scope
Preconditions: Chief profile registered by the Chairman but never nominated (dedicated account)
Steps: 1) Sign in as that chief; 2) GET /api/v1/chief/summary; 3) Open the workspace
Expected Result: ready=false, subjects empty, restricted modules show a locked or empty state and no error dialog renders
Notes: Verify ready=false and that restricted workspaces render a locked or empty state; requires a second chief account registered but never nominated

Title: Sign out revokes the Chief session
Preconditions: Chief signed in
Steps: 1) Click Sign out in the banner; 2) Replay GET /api/v1/chief/summary with the previous cookies
Expected Result: Session ends, the login page returns and the replayed request gets 401/403
Notes: Prompts section 5; reuse the shared logout coverage

Title: Idle session timeout ends the Chief session
Preconditions: Admin policy session_timeout_minutes set to a short value for the test tenant
Steps: 1) Sign in as Chief; 2) Leave the workspace idle past the policy timeout; 3) Perform a protected read
Expected Result: Chief is returned to sign-in and the protected read is refused
Notes: Verify the effective timeout value first; do not hard-code multi-hour waits

Title: A pending nomination blocks the restricted scope
Preconditions: Chairman nominated the chief; the nomination is still pending
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/chief/summary; 2) Read ready and subjects
Expected Result: ready=false and subjects is empty while the nomination is pending
Test Data: chief account with a pending nomination
Notes: Spec CHF-10

Title: Own pending nomination is reported as acceptable
Preconditions: Same pending nomination as CHF-014
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/chairman/my-nominations; 2) Inspect the pending row
Expected Result: status=pending, can_accept=true, blocked_reason empty and nominated_at set
Notes: Spec CHF-11

Title: Accepting the nomination unlocks the chief subject scope
Preconditions: CHF-015 satisfied; DVS_ALLOW_WRITES=true
Steps: 1) POST /api/v1/chairman/nominations/{nominationId}/accept; 2) GET /api/v1/chief/summary
Expected Result: Accept response status=completed; summary ready=true with at least one subject in scope
Test Data: nomination id from the run state
Notes: Spec CHF-12; write-gated to avoid changing shared tenant state

Title: Re-accepting a completed nomination is refused
Preconditions: CHF-016 completed
Steps: 1) POST the accept route again for the same nomination; 2) Re-read my-nominations
Expected Result: 400/403/409; status stays completed and accepted_at is unchanged
Notes: Spec CHF-13

Title: Accepting a nomination that belongs to another chief is refused
Preconditions: A nomination exists for a different chief of the same subject
Steps: 1) POST accept for the foreign nomination id; 2) Re-read the foreign nomination as its owner
Expected Result: 403; the foreign nomination is unchanged and the caller scope stays locked
Notes: Spec CHF-14 only probes a zero uuid; a real foreign nomination id is the stronger isolation check

Title: Accepting an unknown nomination id is refused
Preconditions: Chief signed in
Expected Result: 400/403/404/409 and no nomination row is created
Notes: Spec CHF-14

Title: A blocked nomination cannot be accepted
Preconditions: A nomination row exists with can_accept=false and a non-empty blocked_reason
Steps: 1) POST accept for that nomination; 2) Re-read the nomination
Expected Result: Refused with 4xx; status and accepted_at unchanged; blocked_reason still reported
Notes: Verify which condition blocks acceptance and that the API, not only the UI, refuses it

Title: Chief cannot create a nomination through the chairman route
Preconditions: Chief signed in with an unlocked scope; a second evaluator profile exists
Steps: 1) POST /api/v1/chairman/nominations with the evaluator and subject ids; 2) Read my-nominations
Expected Result: 403; no nomination row is created for the caller
Notes: Confirm the role guard on CHAIRMAN_NOMINATIONS for the chief role

Title: Simultaneous double accept yields exactly one completion
Preconditions: A pending nomination for the chief; disposable tenant data
Steps: 1) Fire two accept POSTs for the same nomination in parallel; 2) Re-read the nomination and the summary
Expected Result: One request completes the row and the other receives 4xx/409; exactly one accepted_at and one completed transition
Test Data: same nomination id, two parallel requests
Notes: Assert on the persisted row rather than on response ordering

Title: Accept retried after a client timeout does not double-apply
Preconditions: A pending nomination; a client able to abort mid-flight
Steps: 1) Send accept and abort the connection after the request reaches the server; 2) Resend the same accept
Expected Result: The nomination is completed once and the retry is refused or returns the same completed state
Notes: Abort with an API context timeout; verify no second state transition in the audit history

Title: The accepted nomination state is durable
Preconditions: CHF-016 completed
Steps: 1) Sign out and sign in again as the chief; 2) Re-read my-nominations and chief summary
Expected Result: status completed, accepted_at set, and the subject still present in the chief summary after re-login
Notes: Spec CHF-12/13 re-check the summary in-session; add the re-login read

Title: Evaluator profile is registered from the master with the required profile block
Preconditions: Chief scope unlocked; subject accepted
Steps: 1) Open Evaluator master; 2) Register evaluator with full name, email, institution, department and experience; 3) Continue, select the subject, register
Expected Result: Profile is created and the response reports role=evaluator
Test Data: display_name DVS Evaluator RUNID; email dvs.evaluator.tc.TS@example.com; institution DVS Automation Institute; department CSE; years_experience 5; subject KAN001
Notes: Spec CHF-20 (POST /api/v1/evaluator-management)

Title: New evaluator profile carries the evaluator role only
Preconditions: CHF-025 completed
Steps: 1) Read the create response; 2) Read the Evaluator master list
Expected Result: role=evaluator, grade is not chief, and the profile is listed once in the master
Notes: Spec CHF-20 asserts role; add the master-list read

Title: Registration does not enable login; the handover is issued only on nomination
Preconditions: Chief scope unlocked
Steps: 1) Register an evaluator choosing the Later login option; 2) Inspect login_enabled; 3) Attempt to sign in as that evaluator
Expected Result: Login is not enabled, sign-in is refused and no temporary password is handed over at registration
Test Data: evaluator registered with the Later option
Notes: Section 13.2 offers Create login and issue a temporary password or Later; verify login_enabled=false and that no credentials are returned

Title: The optional profile block may be omitted
Preconditions: Chief scope unlocked
Steps: 1) Register with only full name, email, institution, department and experience
Expected Result: Profile is created with mobile, employee_id, designation, qualification and employment_type empty
Notes: Verify which of the section 12.2 optional fields the Evaluator master treats as optional

Title: A duplicate evaluator email is rejected
Preconditions: An evaluator was registered in this run
Steps: 1) Register a second evaluator reusing the first email
Expected Result: 4xx with a field error; the first profile stays the only record
Notes: Spec CHF-24 sends a fresh email for the duplicate probe; tighten it to reuse the first email

Title: A missing display name is rejected
Preconditions: Chief scope unlocked
Steps: 1) POST evaluator-management without display_name
Expected Result: 4xx with a field-level error; nothing is created
Notes: Verify display_name is mandatory for the chief role on EVALUATOR_MANAGEMENT

Title: An invalid email format is rejected
Preconditions: Chief scope unlocked
Steps: 1) POST evaluator-management with a malformed email
Expected Result: 4xx with a field-level error; nothing is created
Notes: Confirm server-side email validation rather than UI-only validation

Title: Experience boundary values are handled consistently
Preconditions: Chief scope unlocked
Steps: 1) Register with years_experience 0; 2) Register with an implausible upper value; 3) Read the profiles
Expected Result: 0 is accepted as a valid boundary and the upper value is either rejected or stored consistently, with the same rule on both paths
Notes: No documented range exists; establish the accepted bounds before asserting. Negative values are covered by the Chairman suite

Title: Chief cannot register an evaluator for a subject outside the accepted scope
Preconditions: Chief scope contains a single accepted subject
Steps: 1) POST evaluator-management with an unrelated subject id
Expected Result: 403/4xx; no profile is created and the scope is unchanged
Notes: Verify a 403/4xx for an out-of-scope subject id; docs/testcases/04-chief-examiner.md marks CHF-25 Automated but the spec has no such case, so add the coverage

Title: Chief cannot create a chief-grade profile through the evaluator master
Preconditions: Chief scope unlocked
Steps: 1) POST evaluator-management including a chief grade or equivalent privilege field
Expected Result: 4xx/403; no chief-grade profile is created by a chief
Notes: Verify whether grade is accepted on the chief's evaluator-management payload and that it cannot be escalated

Title: Editing an evaluator profile persists
Preconditions: CHF-025 completed; Edit profile available
Steps: 1) Open Edit profile; 2) Change designation and qualification; 3) Save; 4) Reload the list
Expected Result: The new values persist; email and evaluator_code are unchanged
Test Data: designation Assistant Professor to Associate Professor
Notes: Verify the edit persists and that email and evaluator_code stay immutable; Edit profile is documented in section 13.2 but no page object exists yet

Title: Deactivating an evaluator removes them from allocation eligibility
Preconditions: CHF-025 completed; the evaluator is not allocated
Steps: 1) Deactivate the evaluator; 2) Read batch members and available_candidates
Expected Result: The evaluator is no longer offered as an allocation candidate and keeps their history
Notes: Deactivate is documented in section 13.2; verify behaviour when an in-flight assignment exists

Title: Selected subject expertise persists exactly
Preconditions: Two subjects selectable through Select visible or filters
Steps: 1) Select two subjects; 2) Register; 3) Re-read the profile and the team entry
Expected Result: Exactly the selected subject ids are stored, with no implicit extras and no drops
Test Data: subject ids from the accepted scope
Notes: Verify filters and Select visible cannot select subjects outside the chief scope

Title: Evaluator master list stays responsive for a large team
Preconditions: 50 evaluator profiles registered for the chief
Steps: 1) Load Evaluator master; 2) Load Manage team; 3) Time both reads
Expected Result: Both surfaces return inside the configured timeout with no pagination stall
Notes: Verify the measured duration with 50 evaluators seeded and record it as the performance baseline

Title: Registration alone does not add team membership
Preconditions: Evaluator registered in CHF-025 but not nominated
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/evaluator-management/chiefs/me/team
Expected Result: The evaluator is absent from assigned_evaluators and may appear in available_candidates with is_assigned=false
Notes: Spec CHF-21

Title: Nomination returns the handover and marks the evaluator nominated
Preconditions: CHF-025 completed; chief scope unlocked
Steps: 1) POST /api/v1/chief/team/nominations with evaluator_id and subject_id
Expected Result: nominated=true and credentials.username plus credentials.temporary_password are present once
Notes: Spec CHF-22; the temporary password must never be logged, persisted or attached to a report

Title: The nominated evaluator appears in the chief team
Preconditions: CHF-041 completed
Steps: 1) GET the chief team; 2) Validate the payload
Expected Result: assigned_evaluators contains the evaluator with evaluator_code, grade, institution_name and the subject entry
Notes: Spec CHF-23

Title: The team list keeps one row per evaluator across repeated reads
Preconditions: At least two nominated evaluators
Steps: 1) Read the team three times; 2) Compare the member sets and ids
Expected Result: The same member set is returned each time with no duplicate evaluator_id rows
Notes: Repeat-read consistency, mirrors spec CHF-61

Title: A duplicate nomination for the same subject is refused or idempotent
Preconditions: CHF-041 completed
Steps: 1) POST the same nomination again; 2) Read the team
Expected Result: 4xx or the same nomination state; exactly one team row remains
Notes: The Chairman suite covers duplicate nomination for chiefs; the chief-to-evaluator path is unverified

Title: Nominating an unknown evaluator id is refused
Preconditions: Chief scope unlocked
Steps: 1) POST chief/team/nominations with 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
Expected Result: 4xx; nothing is added to the team
Notes: Add the probe to the existing nomination test

Title: Nominating into a subject outside the accepted scope is refused
Preconditions: A registered evaluator; a subject outside the chief scope
Steps: 1) POST chief/team/nominations with the foreign subject id
Expected Result: 403/4xx; no membership is created
Notes: Confirm the server enforces the scope, not only the UI subject picker

Title: Nominating an evaluator already held by another chief is refused
Preconditions: available_candidates contains a row with is_assigned=true and current_chief_id set
Steps: 1) Read the candidate list; 2) Attempt the nomination
Expected Result: Refused with the owning chief visible; the foreign team is unchanged
Notes: Verify the server refuses the nomination and names the owning chief; available_candidates already exposes is_assigned and current_chief_name, so the UI should block before the API call

Title: The candidate list exposes foreign membership and capacity
Preconditions: Chief team route readable
Steps: 1) GET the chief team; 2) Inspect available_candidates
Expected Result: Each candidate carries is_assigned, current_chief_id, current_chief_name, grade, daily_capacity and subjects
Notes: Schema-grounded field assertions

Title: Allocation is refused when the evaluator has no recorded attendance
Preconditions: A ready packet exists; the selected member has present=false
Steps: 1) POST /api/v1/allocation/examiner-batches/{batchId}/allocate-subject-group for the absent member
Expected Result: 403 whose message names the presenter/attendance gate and no assignment is created
Test Data: group_id of the ready packet; member_id of an absent evaluator
Notes: Spec CHF-31 accepts 200/201/403/409, which masks a missing gate; tighten to 403 plus a zero assignment count

Title: The batch member shows packet unavailability before attendance
Preconditions: An evaluator in the batch without presence
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/allocation/examiner-batches; 2) Read members[].packet_available and packet_blocker
Expected Result: packet_available=false with a non-empty packet_blocker for the absent evaluator
Notes: Spec CHF-32 asserts the property exists; add the value assertions

Title: Allocation succeeds once attendance is recorded
Preconditions: The evaluator completed the face step; the packet is ready
Steps: 1) POST allocate-subject-group for the present member; 2) Read the evaluator assignment catalog
Expected Result: 200/201 and one assignment per script of the packet for that evaluator
Notes: Chain step allocateToEvaluator in utils/evaluationCompletion.ts

Title: A plain login does not create presence
Preconditions: Evaluator signed in but the face step not completed
Steps: 1) Sign in as the evaluator; 2) Read attendance in the chief summary and the batch members
Expected Result: present=false and packet unavailable; authentication alone never grants presence
Notes: Spec CHF-50 only asserts the packet_available property; the real check needs the human face step in a headed browser

Title: Attendance reports presence and per-session check-ins
Preconditions: At least one evaluator completed the live face step
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/chief/summary; 2) Inspect attendance[] and the present counter
Expected Result: Each evaluator carries present and checkins[] with session, checked_in_at and present; the present counter equals the number of present evaluators
Notes: Check-in rows only exist after the human face step; the read itself is scriptable

Title: An expertise mismatch blocks allocation for that subject
Preconditions: A member whose eligible_subject_ids exclude the packet subject
Steps: 1) Read subject_availability for that subject; 2) Attempt the allocation
Expected Result: packet_available=false for that subject with a blocker and the allocation is refused
Notes: Verify the blocker wording for an expertise mismatch versus an attendance blocker

Title: An evaluator holding an active packet cannot receive a second packet
Preconditions: An evaluator is already allocated a packet that is not finished
Steps: 1) Attempt to allocate a second packet to that member
Expected Result: Refused with an active-packet blocker and no second assignment set
Test Data: second ready group_id plus the busy member id
Notes: Prompts section 13.4 step 7 lists the active packet as an eligibility blocker; no automated assertion exists

Title: The Attendance module lists the chief team with presence state
Preconditions: Chief signed in; team nominated; at least one face step completed
Steps: 1) Open Attendance; 2) Compare the rows with the chief summary attendance
Expected Result: The same evaluators appear with a presence state that matches the summary
Test Data: chief summary attendance[] vs the Attendance surface
Notes: Attendance labels are documented in section 21 but no page object exists; verify the row set after a live face step

Title: A failed attendance read never grants presence
Preconditions: A proxied or blocked attendance/summary response
Steps: 1) Fail or time out the attendance read; 2) Attempt an allocation for an absent member
Expected Result: The allocation is refused and the failure is surfaced; presence is never assumed on error
Notes: Use Playwright route interception to fail the call; confirm the UI surfaces an error rather than defaulting to present

Title: A submitted packet appears ready for allocation
Preconditions: The scanner submitted the packet for the chief's paper
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/allocation/examiner-batches/{batchId}/subject-groups
Expected Result: group ready=true, submitted=true, closed=true and stored_count equals total_count and packet_size
Notes: Spec CHF-30 only asserts ready and submitted; add the count equality

Title: Allocation assigns the whole packet to one evaluator
Preconditions: CHF-051 completed
Steps: 1) Read the evaluator assignment catalog; 2) Map every script of the group to its evaluator
Expected Result: Every script in the group has the same evaluator_id and valuation_round; no partial assignment
Notes: docs/testcases/04-chief-examiner.md CHF-34 states this outcome but the spec never compares per-script evaluators; add it

Title: The allocate response accounts for every script
Preconditions: A ready packet and an eligible member
Steps: 1) POST allocate-subject-group; 2) Inspect group_id, allocated_count, ai_queued_count and assignments
Expected Result: allocated_count equals the packet size, assignments length equals allocated_count and every assignment id is unique
Notes: Schema-grounded; add to the allocation test

Title: Re-allocating an allocated packet is refused or idempotent
Preconditions: CHF-051 completed
Steps: 1) POST the same group and member again; 2) Recount the group's assignments
Expected Result: 4xx or the same assignment set; the assignment count stays equal to packet_size
Notes: Spec CHF-35; add the unchanged-count assertion

Title: A packet that is not submitted cannot be allocated
Preconditions: A group with submitted=false in the chief batch
Steps: 1) POST allocate-subject-group for that group
Expected Result: 4xx and no assignment is created
Notes: Verify a 4xx and zero assignments; requires an open or partial packet from the scanner

Title: A member id outside the batch is refused
Preconditions: A member id from a different batch
Steps: 1) POST allocate-subject-group with the foreign member id
Expected Result: 4xx and nothing is assigned
Notes: Verify the status and message and that no assignment is created; this is the boundary between a validation failure and a cross-batch escalation

Title: An unknown batch id is refused
Preconditions: Chief signed in
Expected Result: 400/403/404 with no assignment created
Notes: Spec CHF-36

Title: A foreign chief's batch cannot be allocated to this chief's member
Preconditions: Two chiefs with batches on the same tenant
Steps: 1) POST allocate-subject-group on the foreign batch id with this chief's member id
Expected Result: 403; no cross-batch assignment exists afterwards
Test Data: foreign batch id plus own member id
Notes: docs/testcases/04-chief-examiner.md marks CHF-36 Automated, but the spec only probes a zero uuid; a real second-chief batch is the actual isolation test

Title: A member_id from another batch cannot be injected into own batch allocation
Preconditions: Own ready packet; a member id belonging to a foreign batch
Steps: 1) POST allocate-subject-group on own batch with the foreign member id
Expected Result: Refused; batch membership and evaluator ownership are validated server-side
Test Data: own batch id plus foreign member id
Notes: Verify server-side membership validation and pair with CHF-065 to distinguish a validation error from a cross-batch escalation

Title: A packet below packet size is not ready
Preconditions: A group where stored_count is below packet_size
Steps: 1) Read subject-groups; 2) Attempt the allocation
Expected Result: ready=false and the allocation is refused with the stored versus total evidence
Notes: Requires a partially stored packet; confirm ready is false rather than merely displayed as such

Title: A packet above its total count is rejected or flagged
Preconditions: A group where stored_count exceeds total_count
Steps: 1) Read subject-groups; 2) Attempt the allocation
Expected Result: 4xx or an explicit over-count warning; scripts are never over-allocated
Notes: Confirm which side wins: stored_count or total_count

Title: Two simultaneous allocations of one packet yield a single assignment set
Preconditions: A ready packet and two eligible members
Steps: 1) Fire two allocate-subject-group POSTs in parallel; 2) Recount the assignments
Expected Result: One request succeeds, the other gets 4xx/409, and the total assignments equal packet_size
Test Data: same group_id, two different member ids
Notes: Highest-risk double-allocation case; assert the persisted assignments, not the responses

Title: Concurrent allocations of two packets in one batch stay independent
Preconditions: Two ready packets and two eligible members
Steps: 1) Allocate both packets in parallel; 2) Read both assignment sets
Expected Result: Both succeed with disjoint assignment sets and the correct evaluator on each packet
Test Data: two group ids, two member ids
Notes: Confirms the allocation lock is per packet, not per batch

Title: Retrying an allocation after a client timeout does not duplicate assignments
Preconditions: A ready packet; a client that can abort mid-flight
Steps: 1) Send the allocation and abort after the request reaches the server; 2) Resend the same allocation
Expected Result: Idempotent outcome; the assignment count still equals packet_size
Notes: Verify an idempotent outcome with the assignment count unchanged; pair with CHF-071 to separate double-submit from retry semantics

Title: The subject-groups read stays inside the configured timeout
Preconditions: A batch holding many subject groups
Steps: 1) GET subject-groups for the batch; 2) Record the duration
Expected Result: The response returns inside the configured timeout and the batch select still renders
Notes: Verify the measured duration for a batch with about 40 subject groups; spec CHF-60 documents the intent but a seeded batch is required to measure it

Title: The Packet allocated dialog confirms and Stay here keeps the batch view
Preconditions: An eligible packet and evaluator selected in the Allocation engine
Steps: 1) Click Allocate packet; 2) Read the dialog; 3) Click Stay here
Expected Result: A dialog containing Packet allocated appears with a Stay here action; the batch view remains and the packet leaves the select
Notes: Grounded in the existing page object; assert the packet disappears from the select after allocation

Title: The examiner batch list contains only this chief's batches
Preconditions: Two chiefs with batches on the same tenant
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/allocation/examiner-batches; 2) Compare every chief.id with the caller profile id
Expected Result: Every returned batch has chief.id equal to the caller and no foreign batch, member or subject is returned
Notes: utils/evaluationCompletion.ts filters by chief.id, implying server scoping; assert it instead of filtering client-side

Title: Subject groups of a foreign chief's batch are refused
Preconditions: A batch id belonging to another chief
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/allocation/examiner-batches/{foreignBatchId}/subject-groups
Expected Result: 403/404; no group, paper, centre or count data is disclosed

Title: Another chief's team cannot be read
Preconditions: A second chief with a nominated team
Steps: 1) GET the chief team route; 2) Attempt any id-based team read that the API exposes
Expected Result: The team route returns only the caller's team and any foreign team read is refused
Notes: The captured route is self-scoped (/chiefs/me/team); assert team.chief.id equals the caller and probe whether an id-based variant exists

Title: A foreign moderation operation cannot be decided
Preconditions: An approved or pending operation owned by another chief
Steps: 1) POST /api/v1/phase4/moderation/operations/{foreignOperationId}/decision
Expected Result: 403/404; the foreign operation keeps its status and version
Test Data: foreign operation id with the current version
Notes: Confirm the decision route resolves ownership, not only existence

Title: Moderation selection on a foreign batch is refused
Preconditions: Another chief's evaluated batch id
Steps: 1) POST /api/v1/phase4/assessment-control/batches/{foreignBatchId}/moderation-selection with record ids
Expected Result: 403; no moderation operation is created and no foreign script content is returned
Test Data: foreign batch id plus arbitrary record ids
Notes: Verify the selection validates record ownership and refuses a foreign batch

Title: A chief session from tenant A is refused on tenant B
Preconditions: Two synthetic universities with a chief account on each
Steps: 1) Sign in as the chief on tenant A; 2) Replay GET /api/v1/chief/summary against tenant B with the tenant A session and tenant header
Expected Result: 401/403; no tenant A data is disclosed by tenant B
Test Data: WEB_APP_URL of tenant B; X-Tenant-Id of tenant A
Notes: Verify 401/403 across tenants; requires the second university described in prompts section 6

Title: Evaluator credentials cannot read chief routes
Preconditions: A nominated evaluator account
Steps: 1) Sign in as the evaluator; 2) GET /api/v1/chief/summary; 3) POST /api/v1/chief/team/nominations; 4) GET /api/v1/allocation/examiner-batches
Expected Result: 403 on every chief route with no chief data disclosed

Title: The assignment viewer is scoped to owned assignments
Preconditions: One assignment in own batch and one foreign assignment id
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/allocation/assignments/{ownId}/viewer?low_bandwidth=false; 2) Repeat with the foreign id
Expected Result: The own assignment returns script and paper data; the foreign id is refused with no script content
Notes: Verify the foreign assignment id is refused; the viewer returns page images, so a leak is a direct script-confidentiality breach

Title: Face and identity status of an evaluator outside the team is not readable
Preconditions: An own-team evaluator and a foreign evaluator
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/evaluator-management/face/status for the caller; 2) Probe the same route with a foreign evaluator reference
Expected Result: Own-team status is readable; a foreign evaluator's identity status is refused or empty
Notes: The captured call is self-scoped; confirm whether an evaluator identifier is accepted before asserting refusal

Title: Chairman-only routes are refused to the chief
Preconditions: Chief signed in
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/chairman/catalog?subject_id={subjectId}; 2) GET /api/v1/chairman/history; 3) GET /api/v1/chairman/my-nominations
Expected Result: 403 on the catalogue and history with no programme-wide data disclosed; my-nominations returns only the caller's own rows
Notes: Verify 403 on the chairman catalogue and history while my-nominations stays readable by the nominee

Title: The admin exam-configuration catalogue is refused to the chief
Preconditions: Chief signed in
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/configuration/catalog?table_key=papers&table_offset=0&table_limit=10
Expected Result: 403; no programme, paper or subject configuration rows are disclosed
Notes: Confirms the chief has no configuration-plane access, matching the module-scope assertion in CHF-003

Title: Workflow reports of another chief's group are not disclosed
Preconditions: Reports exist for two chiefs
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/evaluation-workflow/catalog; 2) Attempt to read a foreign report by id
Expected Result: Only own-group reports are listed and a foreign report id is refused
Notes: Verify report scoping by attempting a foreign report id; report rows carry evaluator and group ids, so scoping must be server-enforced

Title: A submitted evaluation appears as a moderation source
Preconditions: The evaluator submitted at least one script for the chief's paper
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/phase4/catalog?section=assessment; 2) Look for moderation_sources for the paper
Expected Result: The submitted work is listed as a moderation source for the chief's paper
Notes: Spec CHF-40; requires the evaluator submission step to have run

Title: Creating the moderation selection produces an operation
Preconditions: CHF-090 satisfied; the evaluated batch id known
Steps: 1) POST /api/v1/phase4/assessment-control/batches/{batchId}/moderation-selection with the script record ids; 2) Re-read the assessment catalog
Expected Result: 200/201 and exactly one moderation operation for the paper is visible on the next read
Test Data: record_ids from the evaluated batch detail
Notes: Spec CHF-41 plus the chain in utils/evaluationCompletion.ts

Title: Approving with the current version completes the operation
Preconditions: An open moderation operation with all samples reviewed
Steps: 1) POST /api/v1/phase4/moderation/operations/{operationId}/decision with version, decision=approve and a reason
Expected Result: 200; status approved or completed and the version increments by one
Test Data: current operation version and an evidence reason
Notes: Spec CHF-42; validate the decision body against the captured operation payload

Title: A stale moderation version is refused
Preconditions: An open operation whose version has advanced
Steps: 1) POST the decision with version equal to the previous version; 2) Re-read the operation
Expected Result: 409 and no second decision is recorded; the stored version is unchanged
Notes: Spec CHF-44 only probes a zero operation id, so stale-version handling is unverified; add a real stale probe

Title: Moderation without a submitted source is refused
Preconditions: A paper with no submitted evaluation
Steps: 1) POST the moderation selection with arbitrary record ids; 2) Read the assessment catalog
Expected Result: 4xx and no empty moderation operation is created
Notes: Spec CHF-45 documents the intent but the automated case only asserts an unknown id

Title: An unknown moderation operation id is refused
Preconditions: Chief signed in
Steps: 1) POST the decision route on 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 with version 1
Expected Result: 400/403/404/409 and no decision is stored
Notes: Spec CHF-44/45

Title: The decision is blocked until every sampled script is reviewed
Preconditions: A moderation operation with several pending samples
Steps: 1) Attempt the decision before reviewing samples; 2) Review every sample; 3) Decide again
Expected Result: The early decision is refused with a sample-completeness blocker and succeeds only after the last sample review
Notes: Behaviour encoded in reviewModerationSamples (utils/evaluationCompletion.ts); assert the refusal explicitly rather than only satisfying it

Title: A sample review stores marks with a version and completes the sample
Preconditions: A pending moderation sample with a viewer payload
Steps: 1) GET the sample viewer; 2) PUT the sample review with version, complete=true and the per-question marks
Expected Result: 200; the sample reports completed and its marks match the submitted evaluation for each question
Notes: Chain step; the viewer supplies sample_version and question ids

Title: A stale sample version is refused
Preconditions: A sample whose version has advanced
Steps: 1) PUT the sample review with the previous version
Expected Result: 409 and the sample keeps its previous state and marks
Notes: Verify 409 for a stale sample version and unchanged sample marks; this mirrors CHF-093 at sample level and needs two writes to the same sample

Title: An invalid decision value is refused
Preconditions: An open operation with all samples reviewed
Steps: 1) POST the decision with an unsupported decision value
Expected Result: 4xx; the operation status and version are unchanged
Test Data: decision value outside approve and rework
Notes: Only approve was captured; establish the accepted decision vocabulary first

Title: A rework decision records the reason and returns the script
Preconditions: An open operation with all samples reviewed
Steps: 1) Decide with the non-approve value and a reason; 2) Read monitoring and workflow counters
Expected Result: The script returns to rework, the reason is stored, and the rework counter and follow-up list reflect it
Test Data: rework decision plus a written reason
Notes: Chief-side rework after moderation was not captured; the evaluator follow-up screen is covered separately

Title: Two concurrent approvals produce one decision
Preconditions: An open operation with all samples reviewed and version V
Steps: 1) Fire two decision POSTs with version V in parallel; 2) Re-read the operation
Expected Result: One 200 and one 409; a single decision is recorded and the version increments once
Notes: Verify a single decision and one version increment when two requests race, as happens with a second chief tab under deadline pressure

Title: Selecting every record creates one operation without duplicate samples
Preconditions: An evaluated batch with several scripts
Steps: 1) Create the selection with all record ids; 2) GET the operation samples
Expected Result: Exactly one operation is created, sample ids are unique and the sample count follows the selection policy
Test Data: all record ids of the batch
Notes: Verify one operation with unique sample ids and that repeating the selection does not create a second operation

Title: A moderation report is created for the group and evaluator
Preconditions: An approved moderation operation for the group
Steps: 1) POST /api/v1/evaluation-workflow/reports with kind=moderation, group_id, evaluator_id and packet_id=null
Expected Result: 200/201 with a report id; kind moderation; group and evaluator match the approved operation
Notes: Chain step chiefModerateAndReport in utils/evaluationCompletion.ts

Title: Sending the report sets it to submitted and delivers it to the Chairman
Preconditions: CHF-104 created a report with status generated
Steps: 1) POST /api/v1/evaluation-workflow/reports/{reportId}/send with the report version; 2) Re-read the workflow catalog
Expected Result: 200; status submitted and destination chairman; the report appears in the Chairman's inbound list
Notes: Chain step; the Chairman forward to Admin is a separate role case in the Chairman suite

Title: Re-sending a submitted report does not duplicate delivery
Preconditions: CHF-105 completed
Steps: 1) POST the send route again for the same report; 2) Recount the reports
Expected Result: Refused or idempotent; exactly one report row and one submission for the group
Notes: Confirm the status transition guard rather than trusting the UI to hide the action

Title: Sending with a stale report version is refused
Preconditions: A report whose version has advanced
Steps: 1) POST the send route with the previous version
Expected Result: 409; the report status is unchanged
Notes: Verify 409 for a stale report version; it should follow the same optimistic-concurrency pattern as the moderation decision route

Title: The chief moderation report summary returns the documented counters
Preconditions: At least one approved operation
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/chief/moderation/report?summary=true
Expected Result: batches, approved, scripts, evaluators and generated_at are present and consistent with the moderation activity
Notes: Spec CHF-52/53 reads the route with 200/403; validate against api/schemas/chief_moderation_report_api_schema.json

Title: A report cannot be created for a group without an approved moderation
Preconditions: A group with only pending moderation
Steps: 1) POST the report create route for that group
Expected Result: 4xx; no report row is created
Notes: Prevents a report asserting moderation that never happened

Title: Report creation retried after a timeout does not duplicate the report
Preconditions: An approved operation; a client that can abort mid-flight
Steps: 1) POST the report create and abort after the request reaches the server; 2) Resend
Expected Result: Exactly one report row exists for the group and evaluator
Notes: Assert on the workflow catalog report count, not only on the response

Title: Live monitoring exposes per-packet progress counters
Preconditions: At least one allocated packet with progress
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/phase4/hierarchy-monitoring; 2) Inspect packets and rows counts and totals
Expected Result: Each packet carries total, assigned, in_progress, submitted, moderation_pending, approved, rework, overdue and rejected, and totals aggregate them
Notes: Spec CHF-52 reads the route; add the field-level assertions

Title: Live monitoring shows help and blocking evidence per evaluator
Preconditions: An evaluator in a secure session with saved progress
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/phase4/hierarchy-monitoring; 2) Read help_open, blocking, last_saved, last_activity and needs_sample_selection
Expected Result: help_open, blocking reasons, last_saved and last_activity are populated for the chief's packets and stay internally consistent
Notes: Field-level assertions on the captured schema; SOS help and blocking are the escalation signals for a chief under deadline pressure

Title: No secure session means no activity evidence
Preconditions: An evaluator signed in but not inside a secure evaluation session
Steps: 1) Read the evaluator's monitoring row; 2) Compare with attendance
Expected Result: activity and last_activity are empty or absent and presence is not inferred from monitoring data
Notes: Confirms monitoring cannot be used as a proxy for attendance, which the allocation gate depends on

Title: Live monitoring is scoped to the chief's own batch
Preconditions: Two chiefs with active packets on the same tenant
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/phase4/hierarchy-monitoring; 2) Compare the chief and evaluator fields with the caller
Expected Result: The role field identifies the chief scope and only own-batch packets and evaluators are listed
Notes: The response also carries chiefs, chief_subjects and nominations arrays; verify these are scoped too

Title: Live monitoring responds inside the timeout for a large batch
Preconditions: A batch with 50 evaluator rows and several packets
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/phase4/hierarchy-monitoring; 2) Record the duration
Expected Result: The response returns inside the configured timeout and the surface renders without a blank state
Notes: Verify the measured duration with 50 evaluator rows seeded and record it for the performance baseline

Title: Chief evaluator history records the actions with actor and time
Preconditions: Evaluator registrations and grade or status transitions exist
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/chief/evaluator-history
Expected Result: history entries carry action, actor_id, aggregate_type, aggregate_id, payload (to_status, to_grade) and occurred_at for the chief's evaluators
Notes: The captured schema exists but no spec asserts the chief's history; confirm the pagination or limit behaviour before asserting counts

Title: Retried writes do not duplicate audit entries
Preconditions: A repeatable state-changing action (allocation or nomination) with an abortable client
Steps: 1) Perform the action and abort the client after the server receives it; 2) Retry; 3) Read the audit history
Expected Result: One audit entry per effective action and no duplicate history rows
Test Data: action payload reused for the retry
Notes: Verify one history row per effective action after an aborted and retried write; duplication would misrepresent who did what during a dispute

Title: The Chief workspace renders in the configured desktop browser
Preconditions: Chief signed in on the project's configured Chromium project
Steps: 1) Open each of the seven modules; 2) Operate the allocation selects; 3) Record any rendering or control difference
Expected Result: All seven modules render and the allocation selects and dialog are operable in the configured browser; any gap is documented rather than assumed
Notes: Only Chromium is configured in this repository; treat Firefox and WebKit as unverified until a project is added

Title: Allocation assigns every group script to one evaluator
Preconditions: Packet allocated to the Evaluator.
Steps: 1) Query assignments for the group; 2) Compare scripts and evaluator ids.
Expected Result: Every script in the group has the same evaluator and no script is unassigned; no partial assignment rows.
Test Data: Group id and evaluator profile id
Notes: Read-only query; assignment table naming to confirm.

Title: Attendance row appears only after the face step
Preconditions: Evaluator completed face verification.
Steps: 1) Query attendance before and after the face step; 2) Compare presence state.
Expected Result: No presence row before the face completion; exactly one present row after it.
Notes: A plain login must not create a presence row.

Title: Moderation decision and sample reviews persist with version
Preconditions: Moderation samples reviewed and decision approved.
Steps: 1) Query the operation and sample rows; 2) Compare status, version and review counts.
Expected Result: Operation is approved/completed at the expected version; every sample is completed exactly once.
Notes: Stale-version decision must not create a second decision row.

Title: 50 evaluators and 100 groups allocate concurrently
Preconditions: A seeded batch with the stated evaluators and groups.
Steps: 1) Allocate all groups in parallel; 2) Re-read assignments and group counts.
Expected Result: No group is split or double-allocated; every group has one evaluator; no 5xx.
Notes: Record the measured p95 and confirm the agreed budget in Notes before gating CI.

Title: Moderation summary over 500 scripts stays accurate
Preconditions: A batch with 500 submitted scripts.
Steps: 1) Open moderation and load the summary; 2) Compare totals with a database count.
Expected Result: Totals match exactly; p95 within budget; no missing or duplicated sample.
Notes: Record the measured p95 and confirm the agreed budget in Notes before gating CI.

Title: Ten times batch volume preserves allocation integrity
Preconditions: 10x the normal batch volume.
Steps: 1) Allocate and re-read every group; 2) Compare counts and evaluator mapping.
Expected Result: No orphan assignment; group counts exact; p95 within budget.
Notes: Record the measured p95 and confirm the agreed budget in Notes before gating CI.
